_purpose: Tool catalog injected into Module 102's PlanningBrief so the LLM picks tool/operation names from a closed set. Edit when you add/remove a tool from the registry.

fs.description: Filesystem inside configured workspace_roots. Concrete file paths only.

metadata_hints.save_under_outputs: metadata.content (str) is the text to write
metadata_hints.read_safe: no metadata; returns content in execution_result

report.description: Drafts a markdown report payload (the fs tool then writes it).

docx.description: Writes a real .docx (Word) file via python-docx.

pptx.description: Writes a real .pptx (PowerPoint) deck via python-pptx.

xlsx.description: Writes a real .xlsx (Excel) workbook via openpyxl.

metadata_hints.save_under_outputs: metadata.sheets={sheet_name: rows[][]} OR metadata.rows[][] for default sheet

desktop.description: Lists/moves/creates/opens/deletes files on Desktop, scoped to workspace_roots.

image_gen.description: Generate an image from a text prompt. Output saved as PNG under outputs/_images/.

metadata_hints.generate_image: metadata.prompt (str, required; vivid descriptive text). Optional: metadata.size ('1024x1024'|'1024x768'|'768x1024'), metadata.model

gui.description: GUI automation. Powerful and dangerous; every op except screenshot routes GREEN.

metadata_hints.keyboard_hotkey: metadata.combo (e.g. 'ctrl+s'). Dangerous combos like 'ctrl+alt+del', 'win+r' are hard-blocked.

_human_DEPRECATED._doc: DO NOT USE. The 'human' tool was removed from the closed-set catalog because planners (especially Gemini) would over-pick `human.request_clarification` for normal questions, and the underlying executor is a MockTool that returns the literal string 'mock_request_clarification' — users see junk. If you need to ask the user something, use chat.answer with a question and wait for their reply. If you need APPROVAL for a risky action, governance Module 103 routes it through GREEN automatically — you don't need to plan it.
_human_DEPRECATED.description: DEPRECATED — do not include in available_tools

memory.description: Agent's persistent notes about the user and the environment. Bounded markdown files (USER.md, MEMORY.md) injected into the planning brief next task. Use sparingly — only for facts that are likely to matter beyond this turn (preferences, project context, gotchas).

chat.description: Respond to the user in natural language. Use this for ANY task that is a question, conversation, explanation, translation, code answer, or general request where the user is not asking you to produce a file/image. The answer text you put in metadata.body is surfaced to the user verbatim as the agent's reply — write the final answer there, NOT a description of what you'll do.

metadata_hints.answer: metadata.body (str, required) is the natural-language answer shown to the user. Match the user's language. Be direct — no 'I will answer your question:' preamble.

web_search.description: Search the live internet via Tavily (preferred when TAVILY_API_KEY is set) or DuckDuckGo (free, no key). Use ONLY when the user asks for current/factual information that requires looking up real-world sources (news, prices, recent events, people, specific facts). The runtime ALSO auto-injects web search results into your planning brief as `web_search_context` when the user's query looks time-sensitive — when that field is present, you do NOT need to plan a separate web_search action; just write the answer with citations.

metadata_hints.search: metadata.query (str, required) is the search query. Optional: metadata.max_results (int, default 5).

skill_manager.description: Procedural memory store. After a non-trivial successful task, you MAY record HOW you solved it as a SKILL_<id>.md so future similar tasks can reuse the approach. The runtime auto-injects the top-3 relevant skills into your brief as `relevant_skills` — DO NOT plan a separate skill_manager.list action just to read them. Only plan skill_manager.create when you actually solved something new+useful AND the task succeeded (BLUE/GREEN route + verification passed). One skill per task max.

metadata_hints.create: metadata.name (short slug), metadata.description (1-2 sentence summary used for retrieval), metadata.procedure (the markdown body, 60-2000 chars), optional metadata.tags (list of str).

session_search.description: Episodic memory across all past sessions. Full-text search (SQLite FTS5) over the user's previous task goals + execution outputs. Use this for explicit recall like 'what did I ask you about Tesla last week?'. The runtime ALSO auto-injects matching past tasks as `prior_sessions` in your brief whenever the user's prompt contains episodic-recall phrases ("remember when", "last time", "上次", "之前") — when that field is present you do NOT need a separate session_search action.

metadata_hints.count: no metadata; returns total indexed task count.
